question.question: How do camera-based and radar-based driver assistance systems differ in poor visibility?

agent.answer:
From your documents: Camera-based and radar-based driver assistance systems differ in poor visibility. Radar-based systems are less effective in poor visibility, as radar signals can be blocked by heavy rain, snow, or fog. In contrast, camera-based systems can still provide some functionality, such as lane departure warning and blind spot detection, even in poor visibility.

Sources: (2021-ADAS-Guide-Preview.pdf, p. 2); (2021-ADAS-Guide-Preview.pdf, p. 3); (2021-ADAS-Guide-Preview.pdf, p. 5); (2021-ADAS-Guide-Preview.pdf, p. 6)

arguments.query: How do camera-based and radar-based driver assistance systems differ in poor visibility?

baseline.answer: From general knowledge (unverified): Camera-based systems, such as lane departure warning and adaptive cruise control, rely on visible images from cameras mounted on the vehicle. In poor visibility, these cameras may struggle to capture clear images, leading to reduced system performance or false alerts. Radar-based systems, on the other hand, use radio waves to detect objects and distance, which can penetrate fog, rain, or other weather conditions, providing more reliable data in poor visibility.
